stemBlocks.value: P, Q and R lie on the same horizontal line with Q between P and R. A vertical mast RT is observed from P and from Q. PQ = 20 m, and the angles of elevation of T are 32° from P and 48° from Q. a) Let QR = x m and RT = h m, and write two equations for h using tangent. b) Hence show that x tan 48° = (x + 20) tan 32°. c) Calculate x and the height of the mast, giving each answer to 3 significant figures.
Think first: Two right-angled triangles share the same vertical side h, so writing h twice and equating is the whole method.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p175-q01 from workbook page 175.

contentBlocks.value: PR = PQ + QR = x + 20, and tan 32° = h ÷ (x + 20)

solutionSteps.instruction: Equate the two expressions for h.

contentBlocks.value: Both equal the same height h

solutionSteps.instruction: Collect the x terms and solve.

strategyBlocks.value: Write h = x tan 48° from triangle QRT and h = (x + 20) tan 32° from triangle PRT, equate them and solve for x, then substitute back for h.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (a) h = x tan 48° and h = (x + 20) tan 32°  (b) equating the two gives x tan 48° = (x + 20) tan 32°  (c) x = 25.7 m and the mast is 28.6 m high (both to 3 significant figures)

whyThisWorks.value: The mast is the common side of two right-angled triangles standing on the same horizontal line, so expressing its height twice creates a single equation in the one unknown horizontal distance. The nearer observation point always gives the larger angle of elevation, which is why tan 48° − tan 32° is positive and x comes out positive. Only after x is known can the height be recovered.

commonErrors.misconception: Using PR = 20 instead of PR = x + 20.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Using PR = 20 instead of PR = x + 20.

commonErrors.misconception: Rounding x to 25.7 before computing h, which shifts the height in the third significant figure.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Rounding x to 25.7 before computing h, which shifts the height in the third significant figure.

commonErrors.misconception: Pairing 48° with the far point P and 32° with the near point Q.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Pairing 48° with the far point P and 32° with the near point Q.

examTip.value: Keep the unrounded value of x in your calculator memory when substituting back — round only the final answers to the stated accuracy.
